newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki ends on stronger note but still jittery.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki ends on stronger note but still jittery.

text.p: Shares recovered in late trade on Friday after wealer-than-expected U.S. producer prices cheered sentiment, but the outlook remained uncertain after three days of profit-taking, brokers said.

The market was two percent down earlier but there was no panic and the HEX index closed up 0.43 percent at 2,959.20, led by strong gains in UPM-Kymmene. The FOX derivatives and portfolio index closed up 0.77 percent at 1,036.16 points.
Volume was a moderate 632 million markka.
"The weaker-than-expected U.S. PPI was good news for the market, shares reacted immediately," one broker said. "Tone is now much better than in the morning."
But there were still jitters though liquidity remained good.
"If the U.S. market gains today, Helsinki will rise next week, but if Wall Street falls again, I would think that the trend has turned lower," another broker said.
Compared to last Friday, the HEX was 0.1 percent lower.

UPM-Kymmene resumed its bull-run and closed lively trade up 3.80 markka or 3.5 percent at 112.30, lifting also rivals Enso and Metsa-Serla after reports of forest industry hopes for higher pulp prices this spring.
Telecoms major Nokia rose strongly from a session low of 310 markka to close off just 0.10 markka at 318.90.

Raision Tehtaat rose 26.00 markka or over five percent to 500.00 in healthy volume after announcing a joint venture with UPM-Kymmene to develop technology for plant sterol, Raisio's key ingredient for its promising Benecol margarine.
